summary: This note describes the Battle of Domstadtl, fought on 30 June 1758 between the Habsburg Monarchy and the Kingdom of Prussia near the Moravian village Domašov nad Bystřicí during the Third Silesian War, part of the Seven Years' War. It was preceded by a minor clash at Guntramovice on 28 June. Austrian forces destroyed a Prussian supply convoy headed for the army besieging Olomouc, which saved the city and forced Frederick the Great to leave Moravia.
one_line: The 1758 Austrian victory at Domstadtl in Moravia destroyed a Prussian supply convoy and forced Frederick the Great to abandon the siege of Olomouc.
key_facts: The Battle of Domstadtl was also spelled Domstadt, and in Czech it is called Domašov.
The battle was fought between the Habsburg Monarchy and the Kingdom of Prussia at the Moravian village Domašov nad Bystřicí.
The battle took place during the Third Silesian War, which was part of the Seven Years' War.
The battle was fought on 30 June 1758.
A minor clash at Guntramovice (Gundersdorf) preceded the battle on 28 June.
Austrian forces were commanded by Major General Ernst Gideon von Laudon and Major General Joseph von Siskovits.
The Austrians attacked and destroyed a supply convoy bound for the Prussian army besieging Olomouc (Olmütz).
The Prussian army was besieging Olomouc (Olmütz) at the time of the battle.
The Austrian victory saved the city of Olomouc.
Prussian King Frederick the Great was forced to leave Moravia as a result of the Austrian victory.
